english.title: Landlord of premises occupied under residential tenancy agreement by adult disqualified due to immigration status
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 33A(1) and 33C of the Immigration Act 2014.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being the landlord under a residential tenancy agreement
relating to premises in England occupied by an adult who was disqualified as a result of their immigration status from occupying premises under a residential tenancy agreement
knowing/having reasonable cause to believe
that premises occupied by such an adult

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 33C(1) and (2) and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
Time limit for prosecutions:
None
